steps.tx: For women with contraindications to exogenous estrogens, the **progestogen-only pill** provides effective oral contraception without thromboembolic hazards. Traditional formulations containing levonorgestrel or norethisterone require strict compliance within a narrow three-hour window daily. Modern desogestrel seventy-five microgram preparations provide a twelve-hour window by reliably suppressing the ovulatory LH surge.
steps.say: Progestogen-only pills avoid estrogen risks and must be taken daily without pill-free intervals.

vis.alt: Progesterone-only pill blister pack and reproductive mechanisms.
vis.caption: Progesterone-only pill blister pack and female reproductive tract mechanisms. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The primary contraceptive mechanism of traditional minipills is **cervical mucus thickening**. Progestins render the cervical secretion thick, sticky, and impenetrable to ascending spermatozoa within two to four hours of ingestion. Because this mucus barrier wanes after twenty-two hours, daily dosing at the exact same hour is critical for maintaining contraceptive efficacy.
steps.say: Minipills primarily thicken cervical mucus, which forms an impenetrable barrier that wanes after twenty-two hours.

steps.tx: Unlike estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, progestogen-only pills represent the preferred hormonal option in **breastfeeding women**. They do not diminish breast milk volume, impair lactation initiation, or alter maternal milk macronutrient composition. Minipills may be safely initiated immediately postpartum or at the routine six-week postpartum visit.
steps.say: Progestogen-only pills do not compromise breast milk production, making them ideal for lactating mothers.

rows: No effect on volume or quality

steps.tx: The most common clinical side effect prompting discontinuation of progestogen-only pills is **unpredictable menstrual spotting**. In the absence of exogenous cyclical estrogen, the endometrium undergoes irregular asynchronous breakdown, manifesting as breakthrough spotting, light bleeding, or complete amenorrhoea. Patients require thorough anticipatory counselling regarding benign bleeding irregularities before initiation.
steps.say: Unpredictable breakthrough spotting is the main side effect and requires reassuring pre-treatment counselling.

steps.tx: Developed in India by the Central Drug Research Institute, **centchroman ormeloxifene** is a unique non-steroidal, non-hormonal oral contraceptive marketed under the trade name Chhaya. As a selective estrogen receptor modulator, ormeloxifene exhibits tissue-specific antagonist properties on the endometrium while displaying weak estrogenic agonist activity in other tissues.
steps.say: Centchroman is an Indian non-steroidal oral contraceptive that acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator.

vis.alt: Mechanism of action of ormeloxifene on the endometrium.
vis.caption: Ormeloxifene endometrial estrogen receptor antagonism preventing blastocyst implantation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The primary contraceptive action of ormeloxifene is **implantation prevention**. By competitively blocking nuclear estrogen receptors in the endometrium, it disrupts synchrony between the blastocyst and endometrial stroma. Additionally, it accelerates tubal transit of the fertilized ovum, delivering it into the uterine cavity prematurely before the endometrium develops receptive pinopodes.
steps.say: Ormeloxifene blocks endometrial estrogen receptors and accelerates tubal transit to prevent implantation.

right.title: Tubal Motility Effect
points: Speeds up ovum transport through ampulla

steps.tx: Under the National Family Planning Programme, the standardized **centchroman dosage schedule** prescribes thirty milligrams orally twice weekly for the first three months. Starting on the first day of menstrual bleeding, doses are taken on fixed days, typically Sunday and Wednesday. From the fourth month onwards, dosing shifts to thirty milligrams once weekly.
steps.say: Centchroman is taken twice weekly for the first three months, then once weekly thereafter.

steps.tx: Because centchroman lacks steroid hormones, it does not alter lipid profiles, blood pressure, or hepatic coagulation factors, resulting in **zero thromboembolism risk**. It is completely safe during lactation and has a Pearl index of one to two. The principal side effect is prolonged menstrual cycles or delayed periods in ten percent of users.
steps.say: Centchroman carries no thromboembolic risk, though it can cause benign menstrual cycle lengthening.

left.title: Safety Profile
points: No adverse impact on serum lipid levels

right.title: Menstrual Effects
points: Reversible return of normal cycles on stopping
